title: User scripts component
body:
### Is your feature request related to privacy?

No, but it could become

### Is there a patch available for this feature somewhere?

No.

### Describe the solution you would like

as some users have said, I also find privacy pop-ups boring, especially google ones, since in my phone they are quite lagged

### Describe alternatives you have considered

initially I thought about reusing the Inject-scripts-for-AMP-tracking-ads-and-video.patch but then I saw that there is the possibility to activate the support for userscripts, which is somehow better because it leaves no trace in the dom, as opposed to that patch.

as a personal test (and also a bit of a challenge) I tried to reactivate user scripts in bromite (https://www.chromium.org/developers/design-documents/user-scripts) taking them from the extensions and moving them to a new one component, managing to make them work (https://github.com/uazo/bromite/blob/gitpages/userscripts_v2.7z my work)
Obviously, as my first test, there is no ui (and by the way it could be quite long to implement it), we could think to proceed in steps.

I wanted to understand if there was interest and, if so, if we wanted to discuss how to implement it, also considering the security aspects, updates and possible integration with chromium developer tools.

current state:
- [x] base code + reading from folder
  - [x] add details for unmatch header
  - [x] bug DOCUMENT_START not work
- [x] preferences (enable/disable)
  - [x] add link to help page (actually https://github.com/bromite/bromite/wiki/UserScripts)
- [x] ui management (enable/disable/remove script) 
  - [x] consider changing proguard settings for R (see https://stackoverflow.com/a/2889844)
  - [x] add icons (enable/disable)
  - [x] disable add button if feature is disabled
  - [x] bug enable/disable need restart
- [x] add script from file dialog
  - [x] remove excessive permissions prompt from filedialog (camera + audio)
  - [x] check how to transform a content:// (URI) to file:// (PATH)
  - [x] get real script filename from a content://
  - [x] when importing from file, skip non ascii chars used in description to prevent [FATAL:web_string.cc(112)] Check failed: ContainsOnlyASCII()
  - [x] reload list after add and show toast with error (check how works CallByNative)
  - [x] check if a file is real user script (es refuse txt without javascript)
- [x] understand if installation from download makes sense (entry point https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/master:chrome/android/java/src/org/chromium/chrome/browser/download/DownloadUtils.java;l=360), actually we have to download the file
  - [x] check how to request permission from the user
  - [x] not working
- [x] add feature flag
- [x] consider if we want to add a way to prevent crash in the startup
- [ ] code cleaning
  - [x] remove unused code
  - [x] remove unused BrowserContextHandle from bridge
  - [ ] try to simply rendering code
  - [x] change all ifdef removing extension word
  - [x] add a flag for logging
  - [x] add file name to pickle (file) so we can log script name at injection time
  - [x] check compiling webview
- [ ] ui management (2)
  - [ ] script details
  - [ ] disable in incognito
  - [x] view source script
  - [ ] check if we can use an "interstitial" page to install a userscript
  - [ ] localize error strings
- [ ] security verification
  - [ ] consider whether to use a sha256 to verify a possible modification of the file without the user's knowledge (if we give the possibility to choose the scripts folder)
  - [x] check if we can deny network access to injected scripts (check ScriptContext)
  - [x] permit only content:// from pickerui
  - [x] block install intent from outside --> no, ask user
- [ ] understand if it makes sense to use zip files (for adding css directly, userscripts.js doesn't support them directly) code https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/master:components/services/unzip/public/cpp/unzip.cc
- [ ] understand if self-updating makes sense
  - [ ] check how the source can be verified (script is unsigned by default)
  - [ ] or enable include metadata support
- [ ] add management in devtools (like snippets, code https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/master:third_party/devtools-frontend/src/front_end/snippets/ScriptSnippetFileSystem.js)
  - [ ] add flag for "fall-back" in devtools (code https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/master:chrome/browser/android/devtools_server.cc)
- [ ] add test cases
- [x] try with v88
- [x] try with v89
- [x] try with v90
- [x] try with v91
- [x] bug  [FATAL:utf_string_conversions.cc(338)] Check failed: IsStringASCII(utf16). Tampermonkey • Userscript Sources
- [x] handling unicode scripts

comments.author: Participant 1
comments.body:
> I cannot see exactly what you changed without extracting it on a branch.

it's because I haven't changed anything, it's all new, taking code from extensions and removing the superfluous, they are not active in android.
it is a new component, like those already found in the base code. I preferred this way, given the need to keep maintenance easy, it is something we can discuss.

> How would this work on Android?

technically the component attaches itself to the rendering process (it is the default behavior of any existing component) and, responding to events in chromium, injects javascript code declaring when and what.
the browser process, via mojo, sends the scripts to the rendering engine, since it cannot access the disk to retrieve any scripts.
all things I've already found, of course, credit to google teams.

Of all this, I haven't done this last thing yet, but the code already provides for it. for now i just statically declared the scripts, you can see it in `components\user_scripts\content\renderer\user_script_set_manager.cc`

What can be injected is visible here https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/master:extensions/common/user_script.h while here https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/master:extensions/browser/extension_user_script_loader.cc and here https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/master:extensions/common/manifest_handlers/content_scripts_handler.cc the classes that loads from file.

> What integration do you mean here?

I mean that it would also be possible to think of adding the control of user scripts through the chromium developer tools, to make their development easier. this is just an idea, I don't know how to do it yet.

comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body:
> I can insert an on/off flag that activates the evals, @csagan5 do you agree? the current extension code uses the page csp, that was my addition

It is not a trivial difference; with a different CSP that means you allow any code dynamically generated by a domain controlled by the author of the script to end up running in your webpages. It would be perfect to steal credentials; while instead with the current CSP only the code in the `user.js` file is the one that runs.

If this option is introduced then we might end up with most of the scripts being created needing `unsafe-eval`, leading to a generally relaxed security measure. What would be the response when people start to get hacked this way?

Perhaps if you can think of a way to grant it to specific scripts, that would be better; but the observation above still applies: my offering an option to remove the sandbox we are encouraging lax security.

To still benefit from the better security I could deactivate the flag after I'm done. There aren't a lot of things that need eval to work so I don't think many scripts would use it. I think the PR is fine as it is.

comments.body:
> @csagan5 any userscript can steal your data. You definitely shouldn't run any scripts that you haven't either written yourself or thoroughly checked.

The `eval` capability is to allow a script which you have not yet read, nor possibly can, because it can be sourced from a third-party website. This is a substantial difference.

Current scenario: you can read the script that you are going to execute, fully.
Scenario with eval: you never know what script is going to be executed.

So, this is not the same: it is exactly the opposite security-wise and the equivalent [ActiveX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ActiveX) on Android.

@uazo since it was not agreed  to add this feature I will not add it for v97 and it is not sure that we will ever add it, I am sorry that you did all the work already before a decision was taken here.

comments.body:
I'm not entirely sure if this is an issue with the User scripts component itself, but it appears to only happen when it's enabled (and currently only with one script): when opening any page in Bromite, then switching to another app/the launcher, then switching back to Bromite, the page just freezes for 20+ seconds. To be more precise, only the displayed web page freezes, the home button and the URL bar continue to work.

I am pretty sure that the script does not contain any infinite loops, however it does contain quite large objects (several megabytes).

Steps to reproduce:
1. Enable *only* [this cosmetic filter script](https://github.com/bromite/bromite/files/8212564/cosmetic.user.zip) in User Script settings
2. Visit any webpage, the script is injected and works fine (it logs to the browser console)
3. Switch to another app (or the launcher)
4. Switch back to Bromite
5. The page is now frozen and doesn't work anymore.
     * The URL bar and home page button of Bromite still work
     * Tapping any element on the page (e.g. text inputs) will lead to the page being unfrozen (not sure if interaction is required for unfreezing), but only after a significant (more than 20 seconds) delay

I took a [performance profile](https://github.com/bromite/bromite/files/8212666/Profile-20220309T083923.zip), it shows a "Long task" taking 24 seconds while the page is frozen. So basically at around 5 seconds I switched back to Bromite and then it started freezing.

perfect.
the problem is the following: every time you open android recents, for some reason I don't understand, chromium generates a temporary mhtml page in `cache/Offline Pages/archives`.

in my version of [Add-history-support-in-incognito-mode.patch](https://github.com/uazo/bromite/blob/next/v99/build/patches/Add-history-support-in-incognito-mode.patch#L1594) I have already removed it for always incognito mode (it is among the things that I have to pull) without finding functions that stop working.

comments.author: Participant 1
comments.body:
I figured out what that code is for.
substantially chromium, when the device goes offline, automatically uses the self-generated pages from the disk cache instead of simply indicating "No internet connection". removing that call, only bfcache is used and not the one on disk.

> > you would remove this also for normal mode to fix this specific UserScripts issue?
> 
> it depends on what we want to do, for me there is no problem in eliminating it.

Considering that we do not fully understand why it is there, I would not remove it until we do. Perhaps it is a mechanism to avoid bloating the `bfcache`. And since this is a specific example of an user script changing the DOM/HTML a lot, I would not change anything yet.

> for me the bfcache has some privacy problems, it would have to be checked, I don't have the elements yet to be able to say for sure. fundamentally it seems to me that it keeps in memory the state of the renderprocess when the navigation is cross domain: my concern is that the state of the javascript variables is also kept making it useless, but only for example, to delete cookies intra-session if the value is kept in a js variable.
> this would render extensions like autodelete cookies (which I have installed on my desktop) useless. think about a search: I click on a site, cookie autodelete deletes the cookies of the search provider but when I go back, the search engine does not use the cookie but a variable and here it has understood who I am anyway.

So the scenario you are explaining is:
1. visit page
2. have it go in the `bfcache` (visiting another page for example)
3. delete all cookies
4. press back
5. verify that a Javascript-stored value from the `bfcache` still contains the original cookie/session ID

I think this is working as intended because "clearing cookies" does not include "destroy my currently loaded pages". In this case the `bfcache` corresponds (roughly) to a page loaded in another tab: why would you want it to be destroyed when clearing cookies?
A "fix" could be to truncate the `bfcache` when cookies are erased, but that would lead to page reloading when you go back (or forward).

How does this behave in incognito? e.g. is the `bfcache` in incognito showing any different behavior? Probably not.
